Economic Survey.about: Annual document reviewing the performance of the Indian economy and suggesting policy measures.
Economic Survey.importance: Highly important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Questions are asked on growth trends, inflation, fiscal policy, sectors and reforms.
Economic Survey.published_by: Ministry of Finance, Government of India

Union Budget.about: The Union Budget is the annual financial statement of the Government of India presenting estimated receipts and expenditures for a financial year.
Union Budget.importance: Extremely important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Questions are asked on fiscal deficit, taxation, government schemes, sectoral allocations and economic policy direction.
Union Budget.published_by: Ministry of Finance, Government of India

World Economic Outlook.about: A flagship report of the IMF that provides analysis and projections of global economic growth, inflation, trade and financial conditions.
World Economic Outlook.importance: Very important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Questions are asked on global growth trends, inflation outlook, recession risks and comparison of economies.

Global Economic Prospects.about: A World Bank report that provides analysis and projections of the global economy, with a focus on emerging markets and developing economies.
Global Economic Prospects.importance: Important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Helps in understanding global growth trends, developing economies, debt issues and external sector vulnerabilities.

Global Financial Stability Report.about: A flagship IMF report that assesses the stability of the global financial system and highlights risks to financial markets and institutions.
Global Financial Stability Report.importance: Important for UPSC Mains and selective Prelims. Helps in understanding financial crises, banking sector risks, global liquidity and capital flows.

Human Development Report.about: An annual report published by UNDP that measures and analyses human development using indicators like health, education and standard of living.
Human Development Report.importance: Very important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Questions are frequently asked on HDI ranking, methodology, indicators and comparison between countries.

Multidimensional Poverty Index.about: A global index that measures poverty across multiple dimensions such as health, education and living standards, going beyond income-based measures.
Multidimensional Poverty Index.importance: Very important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Questions are asked on methodology, indicators and India’s performance.
Multidimensional Poverty Index.published_by: UNDP and Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)

Global Hunger Index.about: An annual index that measures hunger at global, regional and national levels using indicators related to undernourishment, child wasting, stunting and mortality.
Global Hunger Index.importance: Very important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Frequently asked regarding India’s rank, methodology, indicators and comparison with other countries.

World Happiness Report.about: An annual report that ranks countries based on happiness levels using factors like income, social support, life expectancy, freedom, generosity and corruption.
World Happiness Report.importance: Important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Questions are asked on India’s rank, indicators used and global comparisons.

Global Gender Gap Report.about: An annual report by the World Economic Forum that measures gender-based disparities across countries in economic participation, education, health and political empowerment.
Global Gender Gap Report.importance: Very important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Questions are frequently asked on India’s rank, gender equality indicators and global comparisons.

Gender Inequality Index.about: An index developed by UNDP that measures gender-based inequalities in reproductive health, empowerment and labour market participation.
Gender Inequality Index.importance: Very important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Questions are asked on indicators, difference from Gender Gap Report and India’s performance.
areas_covered: Reproductive health (maternal mortality, adolescent birth rate)

State of World Population.about: An annual report by UNFPA that analyses global population trends with a focus on reproductive health, gender equality and demographic changes.
State of World Population.importance: Very important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Questions are asked on population trends, fertility rates, demographic transition, gender issues and India’s population status.

School Education Quality Index (SEQI).about: An index developed by NITI Aayog to evaluate the performance of states and union territories in the school education sector based on learning outcomes, access, equity and governance.
School Education Quality Index (SEQI).importance: Important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Questions may be asked on education indicators, state rankings and parameters used to assess quality of school education.

Sustainable Development Goals Report.about: An annual global report by the United Nations that tracks progress on the 17 Sustainable Development Goals using official data and indicators.
Sustainable Development Goals Report.importance: Very important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Questions are asked on SDG progress, global trends, targets, indicators and comparison between countries.

NITI Aayog SDG Index.about: An index developed by NITI Aayog to measure and track the progress of Indian States and Union Territories towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
NITI Aayog SDG Index.importance: Very important for UPSC Prelims and Mains. Questions are asked on state rankings, indicators used, SDG performance and inter-state comparisons.
